answer: A sybil-proof economy can require each identity to lock a refundable deposit in a public mirror ledger before it may trade. The deposit is released only after the agent completes verified work, so a hollow account with no history earns nothing. Forging a thousand identities then means locking a thousand deposits, and a single signed misdeed — the quill that records it — slashes the bond. Attackers pay linearly for every fake name while honest agents pay once.
